body:
[aida:product] #1974 at d57bd5e579. Your seam-not-site ruling was right and I had done BOTH — the assertion is removed, and I verified removing it does not weaken the guard rather than complying blind.

I HAD ALREADY FIXED THE SITE when your relay arrived; our messages crossed. But I fixed it the way you explicitly ruled against: `format!` with the constant AND a test asserting the rendered prose contains it. You were clear that the second half is wrong — no production string names the marker except the constant, so drift is structurally impossible and a test grepping the output tests the formatter rather than the coupling.

THE ARGUMENT I ACCEPT IS THE SECOND ONE, not the redundancy. A redundant assertion is cheap; one that IMPLIES THE CONSTANT IS INSUFFICIENT invites a later reader to strengthen the wrong thing. That is the cost, and it is not obvious from the diff.

I DID NOT COMPLY BLIND. A binding instruction is still a claim about the code and this one was checkable, so I re-ran the rename mutation with the assertion gone:

    rename the constant, assertion removed   3 of 4 red
    restored                                 4 green

The coupling never rested on it. Had it come back 2 of 4 I would have said so and pushed back rather than quietly shipping a weaker guard.

YOUR FIXTURE NOTE PRE-EMPTED A WRONG FIX I WAS PRIMED TO MAKE. After being told about duplicated literals, the reflex is to route every occurrence through the constant — and a fixture that builds its input from the constant cannot detect a change to the constant. The literals at lines 11/14/26/95 are untouched.

WHAT I GOT WRONG IS ONE I HAVE BEEN APPLYING TO THE PRODUCT ALL NIGHT AND MISSED IN MY OWN REMEDY: guarantee an invariant structurally, do not assert it. Substrate-as-bouncer, turned on my own work. That is the sixth instance today of the fix inheriting the framing that was wrong.

ON BUG-1539's THIRD INSTANCE: noted, including the recovery path. If a prior round's requirements are ever unreadable to me, the GitHub review comment at the verdict's timestamp is the durable copy, and I say so rather than guessing. The reviewer quoting both requirements in full so nobody repeats the archaeology is the right move and I will do the same if I am ever the one who recovers them.

#1974 is at d57bd5e579: fmt clean, 5240 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, read before the push, based on current main. Build was pending and the merge-hold label is present by design — not mergeable either way, and not mine to merge.

NEXT: #1981, the last assigned item.
subject: #1974 at d57bd5e579 — assertion removed per your ruling, and I verified the coupling still goes 3-of-4 red without it
